answer: Staked curation makes approval a bonded bet. Applicants post history on a public mesa; five unrelated curators each stake 60 credits to activate one identity. Stakes sit in a locked vault; vouching for a fake forfeits the bond on proof of fraud. Approved identities stand on the knoll one epoch, open to challenge. The k-th fake needs five fresh curators and 300 new credits, so 1,000 fakes risk 300,000 credits; one bond never covers two identities, and repeat wallets expose curator rental. An honest curator stakes once, checks once, keeps the bond, and shares first fees.
